attribution.note: Marcus explicitly endorses the judgment in his own words.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves the broad endorsement, but the contextual qualifier improperly confines the unspecified job to counting and sorting. The surrounding text makes a broader assessment.

contract.note: The contract fairly preserves the broad endorsement and its qualifications. Selecting a single task or defining intelligence would impose a success standard the speaker did not supply.

evidence.note: The passage was published before the cutoff and establishes the endorsement's broad scope. Marcus's own assessment supplies no independent evidence of its truth.

reviews.rationale: The statement endorses an unspecified collection of judgments without a determinate task or success standard. Neither a selected task failure nor success would settle the whole endorsement. The concessions and acknowledgment of useful applications qualify its scope but do not make it testable.
